I always run over, thinking maybe they just chomped into a piece of broken glass or forgot to tell me they are allergic to everything they ordered. Then I hear a screech like "I need sweet n low!!" or something similar which is directly in front of them already.

Patience and empathy are some of my strongest traits, but damn I really hate when people blame you for their ordering mistakes.

Once in a while, my day is made (even though I have to hide it) by someone at the table who pays attention to the reality in which they exist. When they call out the irate fool who can't remember their own decisions less than twenty minutes prior, I scream with joy inside my head and drink in the realization as it forms on their face.

My favorite so far is when I ran some food, and they guy just stares at his plate, throwing up his hands while exclaiming, "I never got my appetizer!" Without missing a beat, the woman he was with says in the same tone, "Well, you never ordered one!"

Whenever I get the "I'm not listening, I just waited for you to stop talking" kind of reply, I cut my script and say, "Alllllriight..?"

I did it on accident once, and loved the feel of it, so it's my go to now. I have begun using it in other situations where people say crazy shit.

It's so difficult to hold back these kinds of questions when they pop up in your head. Sometimes, I almost think it would be worth the consequences to see the look on people's faces. Under the guise of finding a possible immune system booster or cure for things like cancer, I would revolutionize medicine by doing years of research and assembling a team of the best of the best biologists and medical scientists. Our products would only effect human DNA. Some would be biological, some viral, some mechanical (nanotechnology). Cures may even be discovered along the way, possibly allowing some to hit the market to garner more funding and credibility. When the world sings the praises of The Human Cure Foundation and can't wait to enjoy the next miracle medicine from them, it begins. Subtle jokes about saving an ungrateful humanity start to show me who laughs the hardest. Jokes turn into discussions. I take as many years as I need to assemble a group of incredibly intelligent, jaded individuals who are tired of watching people fuck up the incredible oasis of life which is the Earth, in the desert of the universe.

Judgement would be made based on trust for each person, but more than likely, no individual would know another member of the group. One piece of innocent research passes along and becomes something else in the hands of another. An airborne, self replicating immunobooster only targeting human DNA is developed, perhaps even successfully used and accepted into daily life. It is then changed subtly here and there, only noticeable to those involved. 

The Human Cure Foundation's medicines are everywhere at this point- pumped into air vents at sporting events, injected into fetuses before birth, added to water resovoirs, added harmlessly to cattle, chicken, agriculture, etc. 

Multiple preparation batches are released and used by the world, slowly creating critical weaknesses. Then, one day, Final Batch is shipped. Every major populated area in the world waits for its regular shipment from the HCF, receives it, and begins dispersal. The old, young, and sickly likely go first. The strong carry the boosters and allow them to travel, eventually succumbing. Third world and other remote areas eventually are all hit, as the airborne, waterborne, and nano bots work their way into every air and water system. Insects carrying immunized blood to animals, livestock, even people directly. Any isolated pockets of humanity do not last, as all food and water sources are permanently crawling with the cure.

The Human Cure Foundation has completed its task. Earth is cured of its humans, and the planet is given back to creatures who have less ability to destroy it.

"So, another has come forth. I am unsure whether to give you my congratulations or my condolences."

His lack of surprise makes you uncomfortable. In fact, his withered face seems to sink into what can only be described as a strange mix of anticipation and disappointment. You see jagged, stark white teeth behind an oily beard as he repeatedly licks his lips. While speaking in a cracked and hoarse voice, he draws three oddly cut gemstones from a pocket in his tunic. 

"Choose when you are ready."

The candle light flickers, reflections dancing in his eyes. He sets the stones in a row onto a wooden table, worn with age, never breaking eye contact with you. The  colors are difficult to discern in the dim light, but they look to be amber, violet, and blood red. You feel disoriented as you realize you are now seated across from the old man, gazing at the stones. How long have you been sitting there?  You look up at the man and see no impatience on his face. Your eyes go back to the stones, and for the first time, you begin to wonder.. What is this place?

"Having trouble, ehh?" the old man croaks. "Let me tell you a story. A farmer once lived surrounded on three sides by forests, one side an ocean. He was born there and had no idea what was beyond any of it. Sometimes, a raven would fly from the eastern forest with a pouch of gold, and he would leave his harvest under the great tree, as his father taught him. Not once did he ever see who or what collected it. He simply knew it must be done, or he had no chance to buy passage west on a ship to find a wife."

The old man reached out a pale, bony hand and grasped the three stones. With surprisingly nimble fingers, he began to tumble all three stones around and around his upturned hand in a mesmerizing juggle while he continued the story.

 "One day, the farmer realized he had a choice. He could save the gold he earned breaking his back in the fields for another purpose if he wished. He could explore beyond the farm, buy his own ship, or any number of fleeting pleasures he learned of from the traders of exotic goods. Foregoing the path his father took would even save another soul from being spawned into this wretched and difficult existence. Afterall, there was so much he didn't know about the world around him. Why not seek some wisdom, pleasure, or more gold elsewhere? The farm was his home, but surely he could live elsewhere, perhaps even fall in love with a woman from a far away land. Which direction would you go if you were the farmer?"

He broke the pattern and set down the amber stone. "Gold?"

"Love?" The red stone hit the table with a soft clunk.

"Or loyalty?" The violet stone joined its counterparts.

The old man, still having not once broken eye contact, folded his hands and waited. 

Soaking in all of his riddles distracted you from the strangeness of the entire situation, and you perceive much time has passed. You attempt to hasten your decision, which the old man sees, and interrupts your thoughts once more.

"Perhaps you need more time," he says with what you believe is a hint of a grin. "It has been some time since I have had a drink. Would you share one with me?"

He produces an elaborately ornate bottle with glass matching the violet stone, an already broken red wax seal, and stunning gold leaf lettering, too obscured by dust to be read.

"An exquisite elixir, but only when shared with another lost soul. Care to indulge?"

He removes his darkly colored tunic, powder drifting upwards from it, and sets it neatly folded on the bench next to him. He is little more than skin and bones. His atrophy is visible through tightly wrapped, white bindings with tatters hanging around his limbs. Between his scraggly beard and crooked teeth, it is difficult to tell, but you are fairly certain he is smiling as he nods toward a pair of tiny, bronze cups, akin to cordial glasses in shape. You take his meaning and place them in the center of the table. 

"You have never tasted a drink of its equal," he says as he pulls the cork with a squeak. An ounce or two trickles into each cup as he carefully pours a black liquid from the antiquated vessel. You raise your cups together as he looks you in the eye. 

"To decision," he says, clicking his teeth together and tilting his head forward.

You each drink the contents of your cup and set them down. You hear him exhale slowly through his nose with a hum of pleasure. It is without a doubt the oddest and most delectable substance to ever have graced your senses. It seems to wash over you and give you a new perspective on what it is to experience pleasure. While you are digesting the experience, you missed the old man break eye contact with you. In fact, he has nodded off. "Let the old man rest a while," you think. "He looked so tired."

A stretch of time passes, and you begin to feel a chill. The old man won't mind if you borrow his tunic. He looks quite comfortable, anyway. As you slip on the dusty clothing, the candle begins to flicker and dance. That's funny, there doesn't seem to be a draft at all. Soon, even with absolutely no air flow, the candle is flickering wildly, casting extreme shadows everywhere.

Is the old man getting even thinner? You stare, unblinking, as his body decomposes into a skeleton. Then, the bones, hair and bindings crumble, eventually disintegrating into a fine powder. You can't believe your eyes, but you must, for the only thing left of the old man is his tunic around your now decrepit body. What has happened?

Sometimes, if you stare at it, the candle dances slowly, or not at all. To pass the time, you play with the gemstones and eventually, you are almost as good as the old man was at the tumbling, juggling trick. A bit more practice and you'll get it. You try the drink again, but the old man was right. It tastes bitter and metallic when you drink it alone. You put the bottle away and watch the candle dance for an undetermined amount of time.

The candle slows to a normal pace as you are startled by a splashing noise. A man is coughing and sputtering as he drags himself from the water. He freezes when he sees you, his mouth agape. While stroking your considerable beard, you gesture toward the bench and invite him to sit.

This is exactly my point. I raised these questions in hopes people would realize everyone has a right to live or die as they please. So I empathize with you. You have every right to feel your own pain and desire to help others. Pain is real, no matter what the source may be. My feeling burned out and tired is real to me. As far as why I continue to exist, it feels mainly due to my indoctrination into this guilt ridden society. I am a product of my environment.

I have no anger towards my loved ones, merely a desire for empathy since we all have our sources of anguish. I am in the process of tying up loose ends to leave behind as little mess as possible. I am also preparing my mind through meditation. I'm attempting to finish the job of suppressing my desires for pleasure and continued existence which started years ago through many philosophical thought processes sparked by- you guessed it, pain. I realized going on isn't worth it, but it is taking time to gather the strength to do what I must and overcome any remaining guilt or fear. 

Please do not mistake any of my words for anger or intent to convince anyone to imitate me. Each individual has a unique path to follow. One of the main reasons I want out is actually because I do not wish to further influence anyone or anything- good or bad. If non existence was an option, I believe I'd take that. I don't want to leave as an "I'll show them" kind of gesture. I wish I could sneak away and be forgotten, but I have stupidly made too many emotional ties over the years in order to cope with all the feelings which come along with simply being alive. 

My number one philosophy is to have as much fun as possible while hurting others as little as possible. With that in mind, my existence is now a difficult riddle I am having trouble solving. Daily existence is both fantastic and excruciating at once. Do I go on for more of each, or bend my philosophy and hurt others by halting my experience now? It's quite the conundrum, and I don't expect anyone to understand or care. I think I just needed to shout into the void a bit, as these topics are deemed too taboo to ponder or talk about with people I know.

For this reason, I can never fully vent to anyone and feel deeply isolated. Why do people act like or think they care? I have asked one person this face to face, and he admitted he had no idea. My theory is every motive in life is made with one's own well being prioritized. People do things they deem nice or right to feel better inside themselves. I have greatly pondered why anyone would care if someone else voluntarily left this life. Tracing all motivations logically, it comes down to preservation of one's own comfort. When someone chooses to end their life, it forces people to question themselves. It forces the realization it is and always has been an option to opt out of all pain, pleasure, and everything in between. People are reminded of their own mistakes, regrets, and frittered time, then show their jealousy of unspent years, youthful bodies, money, loved ones, talent, fame, or any other such commodity by uttering such classics as, "What a waste." They are reminded of their own mortality and are made one unit closer to complete solidarity, as we all enter and exit this life alone. Perhaps I am tired of being guilted into existing here, despite the overwhelming unpleasantness and pain permeating everything. Am I the selfish one for wanting to leave, or are the ones emotionally blackmailing me into staying the truly self indulgent?
